It is to proactively generate awareness, interest, and intent among high-caliber talent, long before they enter an interview process.\n\nYou will research markets, design outbound campaigns, test channels, and optimize conversion at every stage; from first touch to recruiter handoff. This is not an administrative sourcing role. It is a high-ownership, metrics-driven function built for someone who thrives on experimentation, urgency, and visible impact.\n\nIf you are energized by building pipelines from scratch, thinking like a marketer, and seeing your work directly translate into hires, this role is foundational to Relay’s growth.\n\nWhat You’ll Be Doing\n\n - Talent Demand Generation: Own talent as a demand funnel: identify target personas, priority markets, and talent segments aligned to Relay’s hiring roadmap. Build repeatable, scalable talent pipelines the way GTM teams build account lists, through research, segmentation, and prioritization.\n\n - Campaigns: Proactively generate high-value talent pools using LinkedIn, niche platforms, referrals, events, and non-traditional channels. Treat sourcing like outbound sales: thoughtful targeting, strong hooks, and disciplined follow-up.\n\n - AI-Driven Scale: Leverage AI and automation tools to scale sourcing, outreach, and research without sacrificing personalization\n\n - Funnel Metrics & Optimization: Own top-of-funnel performance metrics end-to-end; Analyze conversion data to identify drop-offs, test improvements, and increase pipeline efficiency\n\n - Experimentation: Run structured experiments on channels, messaging, targeting, and cadence; introduce at least one new experiment per month.\n\n - Collaboration: Partner closely with Talent Acquisition Partners, delivering calibrated candidates who are ready to interview and move quickly through the funnel\n\nWho You Are\n\n - You have 3+ years of experience in talent sourcing, recruiting, outbound sales, demand generation, growth marketing, or a similarly metrics-driven prospecting role\n\n - You think in funnels, conversion rates, and pipeline health. And you use data to tell the story\n\n - You understand that great sourcing is closer to marketing and sales than administration\n\n - You are a creative prospector who looks beyond LinkedIn and job boards to find and engage exceptional talent\n\n - You are a strong storyteller who can capture attention quickly and articulate why Relay is worth joining\n\n - You thrive in fast-moving environments with high accountability and high ownership\n\n - You collaborate well with Talent Acquisition Partners while owning your lane end-to-end\n\nWhat Success Looks Like\n\n - 75-100 quality outbound reachouts per week with ≥33% response rate\n\n - ≥35-40% recruiter pass-through rate from screens\n\n - ≤5 days to calibrate per new role\n\n - ≥33% of total hires come from sourced pipelines\n\n - At least 1 new sourcing/channel experiment per month\n\n\nTHE INTERVIEW PROCESS\n\n - Stage 1: A 45-minute interview with our Senior Manager, Talent Acquisition\n\n - Stage 2: A 45-minute interview with a Senior team member\n\n - Stage 3:  A 60-minute live session with members of our TA team\n\n - Stage 4: A 45-minute in-person values interview with a member of our leadership team\n\nOur Compensation Approach\n\nWe believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth. Compensation follows impact. As impact increases, compensation grows, and we do not limit compensation changes to a once-a-year review cycle.\n\nThe annual salary range for this role is $85,500 CAD to $104,500 CAD.\n\nFor candidates who demonstrate full readiness for the defined scope of the role, the typical starting salary is $95,000 CAD per year. Offers below this point reflect candidates we believe can grow into the full scope of the role with support and development. Offers above this point reflect impact that meaningfully exceeds the role’s defined expectations or an expanded scope from day one.\n\nWe encourage you to have a conversation with your recruiter and ask questions about compensation throughout the hiring process. For more information on our compensation philosophy and perks and benefits, visit our Candidate Hub https://www.notion.so/Candidate-Hub-1c7da8b7f88580a893f7d7c7852b064e?pvs=21.\n\n\n\nWhy Relay Might Be the Perfect Fit For You \n\n - You push relentlessly for reinvention: You're always asking \"how can this be better?\" -- in your work, in your craft, in yourself. Comfort is a signal to push harder, not coast. You'd rather build something better than defend something familiar.\n\n - You crave autonomy: We trust our team with big challenges and the freedom to solve them. If you’re someone who takes initiative, is comfortable taking risks, and seeks input when needed, you’ll find the freedom here empowering.\n\n - You own your work: You take pride in your work, follow through on commitments, and feel a deep sense of responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks.\n\n - You build with AI, not just use it: You're actively embedding AI into how you work, pushing what's possible, and bringing your team along with you.\n\n - You care about impact, not noise: You care deeply about the substance of your work. You measure success by results, not recognition, and you let your work speak for itself. \n\n - You’re energized by complexity and ambiguity: You enjoy tackling problems that don’t come with a playbook. You’re comfortable building from scratch, iterating as you go, and collaborating to shape the best path forward.\n\n - You seek out feedback: You see directness as respect, not criticism. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.\n\n\n\nWe’re looking for a Strategic Operations Manager - Partnerships to join our team supporting the Partner Sales team to empower accounting and bookkeeping professionals to better serve their SMB clients.\n\nJoining Relay means a unique opportunity to make a huge impact by building a category-defining Partner Program from the ground up. You'll play a pivotal role in Relay's growth journey, defining and developing a critical function that will scale one of our most important growth channels. As a strategic connector, you'll work with cross-functional teams (Partner Sales, Marketing, Product, Data, RevOps, and Engineering) to deliver enablement, data, and operational tools for our partners to succeed and grow. If you thrive on building scalable systems, simplifying complexity, and equipping others with the tools to win, then Relay is the place for you.\n\n\n\nWhat You’ll Be Doing\n\nChannel Strategy & Planning\n\n - Own the revenue planning process for the A&B sales channel, including annual planning, quota design, territory modeling, and headcount forecasting.\n\n - Develop and maintain channel-specific go-to-market frameworks that define how we acquire, activate, and expand relationships with accounting and bookkeeping professionals.\n\n - Identify and drive strategic growth opportunities within the A&B segment and present data-backed recommendations to senior leadership to optimize partner sales in alignment with business priorities.\n\nSales Process & Enablement\n\n - Design, document, and continuously improve the end-to-end sales process for A&B channel reps, from prospecting through close and handoff.\n\n - Partner with Sales Enablement to ensure Sales team has the playbooks, tools, and training needed to effectively engage accounting and bookkeeping professionals.\n\n - Lead pipeline management best practices, deal inspection cadences, and stage conversion optimization using modern B2B go-to-market motions and key revenue metrics.\n\n - Monitor and optimize the partner onboarding journey, reducing time to value and friction points\n\nAnalytics & Reporting\n\n - Build and maintain dashboards and reporting frameworks that provide real-time visibility into channel health, pipeline trends, rep performance, and revenue attainment.\n\n - Conduct deep-dive analyses on funnel conversion, churn risk, partner engagement, and seasonal trends specific to the A&B market.\n\n - Establish and monitor channel KPIs, including ARR/MRR growth, client referral rates, partner retention, and bookings velocity.\n\n - Analyze partner activity, client outcomes, and workflow adoption to uncover insights, including tracking the realized value Relay delivers to partners' clients (e.g., cash flow impact, workflow ROI)\n\n - Use data to inform program improvements, partner segmentation, territory management and strategic focus areas\n\n - Design and maintain a partner-facing dashboard for incentive tracking, performance metrics, and earned rewards, while partnering with RevOps and Data to automate reporting workflows, set topline goals, and integrate performance tracking into internal systems\n\nSystems & Tooling\n\n - Administer and optimize CRM workflows, data hygiene, and automation relevant to the A&B channel (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot).\n\n - Evaluate and implement tools that improve prospecting, pipeline visibility, and partner relationship management.\n\n - Ensure data integrity across all systems that feed A&B channel reporting.\n\n - Own and iterate on tools, systems, and processes to improve partner lifecycle management, drive partner engagement and achieve key revenue driving metrics\n\nCross-Functional Collaboration\n\n - Act as the primary RevOps liaison to the A&B channel sales team, ensuring alignment between field execution and company revenue goals.\n\n - Partner with Marketing to define channel-specific demand generation programs, lead routing, and campaign attribution.\n\n - Collaborate with Finance on revenue forecasting, commission plan design, and deal desk processes.\n\n - Work with Product and Customer Success to surface A&B partner feedback and inform roadmap prioritization.\n   \n   \n\nWho You Are\n\n - You have 4+ years of experience in sales or partner enablement, partnerships, consulting, strategy and business operations, sales operations, or other sales channel-facing roles\n\n - You are a systems thinker with a focus on execution, able to take ideas from concept to launch and scale them effectively\n\n - Strong analytical skills with the ability to turn complex data sets into clear, actionable insights.\n\n - Proficient with CRM platforms (Salesforce and HubSpot) and BI/reporting tools (e.g., Metabase, Tableau, Looker, or similar).\n\n - You are a strong communicator who thrives in cross-functional environments and can translate complexity into clarity\n\n - You are curious about how AI and technology can improve your workflow and constantly explore ways to make partner enablement more scalable and intelligent\n\n\n\nBonus Points\n\n - You have experience working with accounting firms, GTM partner programs, or B2B software ecosystems\n\n - Experience building RevOps infrastructure from the ground up or scaling operations in a high-growth environment.\n\n - Familiarity with data infrastructure and analytics tools (e.g., dbt, BigQuery, Snowflake, Metabase, Looker).\n\n - Experience working directly with AI agents, LLM-based applications, or prompt engineering in a production environment.\n\n - Experience supporting a PLG and sales-assisted hybrid GTM motion.\n\n - Background in fintech or SMB-focused SaaS environments.\n\n - You have worked with SMBs in North America\n\n\n\nThe Interview Process\n\n - Stage 1: A 30-minute Google Meet video call with a member of the Talent team\n\n - Stage 2: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with the Director, Revenue Operations and the Director, Sales\n\n - Stage 3: A 45-minute in-person interview with a member of the Leadership team\n\n - Stage 4: A take-home case study followed by a 60-minute Google Meet video call with our team\n\n\n\nOur Compensation Approach\n\nWe believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth. Compensation follows impact. As impact increases, compensation grows, and we do not limit compensation changes to a once-a-year review cycle.\n\nThe annual salary range for this role is $126,000 CAD to $154,000 CAD.\n\nFor candidates who demonstrate full readiness for the defined scope of the role, the typical starting salary is $140,000 CAD. Offers below this point reflect candidates we believe can grow into the full scope of the role with support and development. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.</p><h1>The Mission</h1><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Our People Team exists to build Relay into a company high-performing, ambitious people actively choose and a place where they do career-defining work. </p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">We are hiring a <strong>People Operations &amp; Systems Specialist</strong> to close our operational gap  and build the technical infrastructure that lets the People team operate at a fundamentally different level of efficiency going forward. <br /></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>The Problem Statement</strong></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Right now, two problems sit on top of each other. </p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">First: our People tech stack is fragmented, data lives in multiple systems with limited connectivity, manual handoffs fill the gaps, and there's no single source of truth for People data. </p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Second: our operational and coordination work (onboarding logistics, systems admin, day-to-day People requests) currently has no dedicated owner, which means it's landing on people whose job is meant to be something else.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">This role exists to solve both, in sequence. You'll own the operational work directly from day one, and as you build the automation and systems layer underneath it, that same work should increasingly run itself. The goal is not to add process, but to eliminate it.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><h1>What You'll Be Doing</h1><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">The primary areas of ownership in this role include, but are not limited to:</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>People Operations &amp; That belief shapes how we build. Design Engineering is a small, deliberate function with a clear mandate: own the front-end across the product, hold a high bar of quality, and raise it over time. The team works directly with product and design, responsible for the UI, the interactions, and the design systems that everything is built on top of.\n\n\n\nWe're expanding the team and hiring two design engineers who will have real ownership across the product. You'll work on the hardest things to get right: the details that make an interface feel intentional, the systems that make quality consistent at scale, and the problems that require someone who thinks in both design and code.\n\n\n\nThis is a formative moment for the Design Engineering function at Relay while it’s still relatively new. The Transaction Monitoring team is why that trust is warranted. Every transaction we review is a decision: hold or release, investigate or clear. Good decisions mean legitimate business owners get their money fast and bad actors get stopped before they succeed.\n\nWe're looking for someone with real transaction monitoring experience who is curious, decisive, and excited to build with AI, not just work a queue.\n\n \n\nWhat You'll Be Doing:\n\n - Review and investigate suspicious activity across every payment channel: deposits, checks, wires, and card transactions\n\n - Make hold/release decisions on flagged transactions, and own them — verify the signals, check the story, make the call. You've made real hold/release decisions, not just escalated them.\n\n - You're curious and investigative. Holding a deposit means a business can't access their money; releasing it means betting your judgment that it's clean. You're comfortable owning both.\n\n - You're a problem solver with high agency. You don't just spot issues — you come with solutions and drive them forward without waiting to be asked.\n\n - You build with AI. You're actively using AI tools in how you work today and you're excited to push what's possible with them.\n\n - You communicate clearly. You document findings well and can present them to teammates, compliance, and non-risk partners like CX and Sales.\n\n - You thrive in a fast-paced environment. You're comfortable wearing multiple hats, handling ambiguity, and adapting as fraud patterns shift.\n\n - You have a growth mindset. We build the technology foundations that make AI and insights possible across the product, and we partner with product teams so they can build quickly on top of them. We also act as Relay's innovation center: running fast, exploratory spikes on emerging technologies to establish what's viable before the company commits to it. That means the work spans both ends of the maturity curve, from hardening infrastructure that other teams depend on to prototyping things that may not exist yet.\n\n\n\nIf you’re excited to tackle new problems and care as much about building strong foundations as delivering an impressive end product, you’ll feel at home on Voyager. Lead the relationship with our PR agency, setting the strategic agenda, driving accountability on coverage outcomes, and ensuring the partnership is pulling in the same direction as internal priorities.\n\n - Monitor and protect brand reputation, with a clear-eyed crisis communications playbook and the instincts to know when something needs to move fast.\n\n - Measure what matters—share of voice, earned media quality, executive visibility, message pull-through, and internal comms reach—and use that data to sharpen strategy rather than just report it.\n\n\n\nWho You Are\n\n - We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.\n\n\n\nWe're looking for a Lifecycle Marketing Lead to own Relay's self-serve acquisition lifecycle, the programs that move self-serve signups from first touch through to registration. Your mission: convert acquisition demand into registered Relay customers, and support the onboarding and activation programs that carry them to first funding and first action. You'll sit on the Lifecycle Marketing team, report to the Manager, Lifecycle Marketing, and partner with Demand Gen, Marketing Ops, Rev Ops, Sales, CX, Product, and Data to turn business priorities into customer journeys that ship and perform.\n\n \n\nThis is a high-impact individual contributor role for someone who can operate strategically, execute with precision, and build from scratch. You'll set the lifecycle strategy for self-serve signups and establish best-in-class practices, while still rolling up your sleeves to launch high-visibility campaigns with urgency and craft. The work you lead will move more new customers to funding and first action, faster, and raise the bar for how lifecycle marketing drives growth.\n\n\n\nWhat You'll Be Doing\n\n - Acquisition Lifecycle Strategy & Ownership: Own the self-serve acquisition programs that take new leads from first touch through nurture to registration. Set the strategy, segmentation, and test roadmap for the acquisition funnel, and own the targets tied to it. Support the onboarding and activation programs that carry registered customers to first funding and first action. Build programs and measurement from scratch where none exist today\n\n - Journey Design: Architect and iterate multi-channel journeys across email, push, SMS, and in-app that move self-serve signups from first touch to registered Relay customers, and support the onboarding journeys that carry them to funding and first action, including re-engaging unqualified demo leads back into the self-serve path. Focus on repeatable infrastructure over one-off campaigns, and keep entry and exit logic clean as customer data flows in\n\n - Data & Experimentation: Run A/B tests with clean attribution from day one, tied to your acquisition funnel metrics: lead → registration, plus the downstream funding and first-action metrics your programs support. Partner with Analytics to define baselines, size opportunities, surface insights, and own reporting for your scope\n\n - Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Product, Demand Gen, Sales, CX, Rev Ops, Marketing Ops, PMM, Data, Design, and Compliance to shape quarterly priorities, align on GTM plans, and turn business objectives into lifecycle programs that ship, while maintaining governance standards for compliance, frequency, and deliverability\n\n - AI Integration: Use AI to speed up analysis, copy development, and experimentation, and bring repeatable patterns the team can adopt\n\n - Documentation & Standards: Maintain clear documentation of your lifecycle programs, experiment specs, and performance logs in Notion, and help raise the bar on QA and craft\n\n\n\nWho You Are\n\n - You bring 4-6 years of experience in lifecycle marketing, CRM, or growth marketing, ideally with a self-serve growth, onboarding, or activation focus\n\n - You have a track record of building nurture and onboarding programs that move funnel metrics like registration, funding, or activation\n\n - You bring strong expertise in customer segmentation, behavioural analytics, and journey design across channels\n\n - You're proficient in marketing-automation platforms and have hands-on experience building in HubSpot, or can ramp on it quickly (experience with Iterable, Braze, or Customer.io a plus)\n\n - You're comfortable in the data layer: you pull and reason about funnel data, write clear data requirements, and self-serve on validation rather than waiting on the data team\n\n - You have strong test-design instincts: you hold a clean control, size a cohort, and avoid attribution traps\n\n - You write strong copy, give creative direction, and hold quality from brief to launch.\n\n - You're self-directed: you take an ambiguous goal, scope it, and ship\n\n\n\nBonus Points\n\n - Experience marketing financial technology products to SMB customers\n\n - Familiarity with in-app messaging tools (Chameleon or similar)\n\n - Technical proficiency in SQL, HTML, and marketing-automation languages; comfort with Segment or a reverse-ETL tool like Hightouch\n\n - Experience using AI tools for productivity or analysis\n\n - Experience migrating or consolidating across marketing platforms\n\n\n\nWhat Success Looks Like\n\n - Funnel Conversion: Measurable improvements across the acquisition funnel you own, lead → registration, with downstream lift in funding and first action\n\n - Clean Experimentation: A live test roadmap with honest reads and clean attribution, where each learning feeds the next test\n\n - Connected Journeys: Lifecycle programs that reduce drop-off between stages and improve time-to-value for new customers\n\n - Operational Maturity: Documented journeys, repeatable QA, and a predictable test and campaign cadence\n\n - Cross-Functional Impact: Lifecycle insights that shape GTM plans, product onboarding, and growth strategy beyond your direct scope\n\n\n\nThe Interview Process\n\n - Stage 1: A 30-minute Google Meet video call with a member of the Talent team\n\n - Stage 2: A 60-minute Google Meet video call with the Manager, Lifecycle Marketing\n\n - Stage 3: A 60-minute live session with members of our Marketing team\n\n - Stage 4: A 45-minute in-person interview with a member of the Leadership team\n\n\n\nOur Compensation Approach\n\nWe believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth. Compensation follows impact. As impact increases, compensation grows, and we do not limit compensation changes to a once-a-year review cycle.\n\n \n\nThe annual salary range for this role is $117,000 - 143,000 CAD.\n\n \n\nFor candidates who demonstrate full readiness for the defined scope of the role, the typical starting salary is $130,000 CAD. You'll be instrumental in ensuring that our product & business teams are empowered with deep, actionable insights, enabling us to make informed, data-driven decisions that resonate with our customers' needs.\n\n\n\nWhat You'll Be Doing\n\n - Collaborating with cross-functional teams by proactively proposing analytical solutions and data insights that drive improvement in key strategic pillars\n\n - Ensuring teams have the necessary data they need to function effectively by identifying and tracking core KPIs on top of building dashboards and reports\n\n - Performing in-depth analysis to drive fresh insights, and inform business recommendations by presenting trends to stakeholders\n\n - Monitoring and evaluating data quality to ensure the accuracy and consistency of data\n\n - Consistently delivering high-quality data models, easy-to-interpret visuals (such as charts, graphs and dashboards), and reports that demonstrate a strong understanding of business needs and objectives\n\n - Apply statistical methods to dissect and interpret data, aiding in the prediction and evaluation of new product features and market opportunities. This includes conducting A/B tests and measuring the impact of product changes on user behaviour\n\n - Synthesize information from diverse sources. Integrate and analyze data from user feedback, surveys, operational metrics, and event logs to connect insights directly to business outcomes\n\n - Regularly reporting outcomes and insights to stakeholders across Relay, including the senior leadership team, providing a clear narrative of the impact on business objectives, thereby influencing future data-driven decision-making\n\n\n\nWho You Are\n\n - You have 2+ years of experience as a Data Analyst, Business Analyst, or in another data-focused role\n\n - You are fluent in SQL, including writing complex queries, working with window functions, optimizing performance, and understanding data warehousing concepts and security best practices. You're able to clearly explain your approach and reasoning, not just produce a working query\n\n - You have experience using business intelligence and data visualization tools such as Metabase, Sigma, Periscope, Mode, or similar platforms\n\n - You have a track record of using data to influence business decisions. You enjoy turning complex analyses into clear, actionable insights that drive meaningful outcomes.\n\n - You start with the business problem before jumping into the data, asking thoughtful questions to understand the context and objectives\n\n - You have experience working with large datasets, from exploration and analysis through to delivering insights. You're comfortable working independently while partnering with cross-functional stakeholders\n\n - You communicate clearly, build strong relationships with stakeholders, and enjoy collaborating across multiple teams\n\n - You thrive in ambiguity and adapt quickly in a fast-paced environment where priorities, processes, and data infrastructure continue to evolve\n\n\n\nBonus Points\n\n - Experience with cloud computing (AWS, GCP or Azure) and familiarity with cloud data warehouse platforms (Bigquery, Snowflake, Redshift, etc.)\n\n - Familiarity with dbt for data modelling, automation, or experimentation\n\n - Experience with a data-oriented programming language  (Python, R)\n\n - You’ve joined a company at its early stages and have seen it through scale\n\n\n\nThe Interview Process\n\n - Stage 1: A 30-minute Google Meet video call with a member of the Talent Team\n\n - Stage 2: A 60-minute Google Meet video call with the Hiring Manager\n\n - Stage 3: A take-home case study, followed by a 60-minute Google Meet video call with members of our Data team.\n\n - Stage 4: A 45-minute in-person interview with a member of our Leadership team\n\n\n\nOur Compensation Approach\n\nWe believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth. Compensation follows impact. As impact increases, compensation grows, and we do not limit compensation changes to a once-a-year review cycle.\n\n \n\nThe annual salary range for this role is $99,000 CAD to $121,000 CAD.\n\n \n\nFor candidates who demonstrate full readiness for the defined scope of the role, the typical starting salary is $110,000 CAD. Offers below this point reflect candidates we believe can grow into the full scope of the role with support and development. Offers above this point reflect impact that meaningfully exceeds the role’s defined expectations or an expanded scope from day one.\n\n \n\nWe encourage you to have a conversation with your recruiter and ask questions about compensation throughout the hiring process. We're looking for a data-driven, detail-oriented problem solver who is excited to build out our compliance monitoring capabilities and strengthen how we partner with our sponsor bank – not just maintain existing processes.\n\nAs a Compliance Analyst, you'll own the development and ongoing management of Relay's compliance monitoring program end-to-end, designing the frameworks, testing, and reporting that ensure our products and operations meet regulatory requirements. You'll also be a key point of contact in managing the day-to-day partnership between Relay and our sponsor bank, ensuring alignment on compliance expectations, exam readiness, and issue resolution. Your work directly shapes how Relay identifies, monitors, and remediates compliance risk while maintaining a trusted relationship with our banking partner, meeting the needs of our fast moving business, and ensuring a seamless customer experience.\n\nAt Relay, your work has real reach – helping millions of SMBs operate safely and confidently, while protecting the integrity of our banking partnership. The ideal candidate is comfortable pitching big ideas, self directing to bring those ideas to life, and holds a high bar for craft, quality, and creativity. \n\n\nWhat You’ll Be Doing\n\n - Develop video concepts rooted in Relay’s brand, product, customer needs, cultural relevance, and YouTube best practices.\n\n - Lead end-to-end production across video formats— scripting, scheduling, shoot logistics, on-camera direction, and editing oversight.\n\n - Source and coordinate talent, freelancers, and production vendors, keeping shoots on time and on budget.\n\n - Partner with Brand, Growth, and Product Marketing to align video with campaigns, product launches, and key company moments.\n\n - Build and maintain production workflows and systems that make consistent, high-quality output sustainable.\n\n\n\nWho You Are\n\n - You have 4-5 years of experience in video production, with meaningful time owning work from concept through delivery.\n\n - Your portfolio shows range—different formats, tones, and audiences—and a clear creative point of view.\n\n - You are already experimenting with and implementing AI solutions to streamline your work and move faster and to fill in content gaps while producing more complex projects\n\n - You have hands-on YouTube expertise: you understand the platform’s algorithm, content architecture, and optimization levers well enough to make intentional decisions, not just follow templates.\n\n - You’re a skilled editor in Premiere Pro, Final Cut, or DaVinci Resolve; motion design or After Effects experience is a plus.\n\n - You’re highly organized and detail-oriented, with a strong ability to manage multiple productions at once without dropping quality.\n\n - You naturally move with a sense of urgency and focus. Video is key to our growth and brand strategy going forward and we need a true owner for the channel who moves with speed.\n\n - You communicate clearly and proactively, flag challenges early, and move work forward without needing close oversight.\n\n - You have a genuine feel for cultural relevance—you know what’s resonating, why, and how to connect it back to a brand.\n\n - You’re comfortable collaborating across functions and presenting work-in-progress to stakeholders with clarity and confidence.\n\n\n\nBonus Points\n\n - Experience creating content for SMB, fintech, or financial services audiences.\n\n - Experience editing video with a high standard for craft: pacing, sound, color, graphics, and captions all matter to you.\n\n - Comfort directing non-actor talent on camera—founders, executives, or customers.\n\n - Experience building short-form repurposing workflows (YouTube → Reels → Shorts → LinkedIn).\n\n - Familiarity with AI-assisted video tools for captions, scripting, or B-roll.\n\n - Motion design or animation skills.\n\n - Experience in SaaS, fintech, or a high-growth startup environment.\n\n\n\nThe Interview Process\n\n - Stage 1: A 30-minute Google Meet video call with a member of the Talent team.\n\n - Stage 2: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with the Director of Brand.\n\n - Stage 3:  A video-focused exercise or case study presented to members of the Marketing team and the Director of Brand\n\n - Stage 4: A 45-minute in-person interview with a member of the Leadership team.\n\nNOTE: All applications must include a link to your portfolio. Applications without portfolios will not be considered.\n\n\n\nOur Compensation Approach\n\nWe believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth. Compensation follows impact. As impact increases, compensation grows, and we do not limit compensation changes to a once-a-year review cycle.\n\n \n\nThe annual salary range for this role is $108,000 CAD to $132,000 CAD.\n\n \n\nFor candidates who demonstrate full readiness for the defined scope of the role, the typical starting salary is $120,000 CAD. Offers below this point reflect candidates we believe can grow into the full scope of the role with support and development. Offers above this point reflect impact that meaningfully exceeds the role’s defined expectations or an expanded scope from day one.\n\n \n\nWe encourage you to have a conversation with your recruiter and ask questions about compensation throughout the hiring process. For more information on our compensation philosophy and perks and benefits, visit our Candidate Hub https://www.notion.so/Candidate-Hub-1c7da8b7f88580a893f7d7c7852b064e?pvs=21.\n\n\n\nWhy Relay Might Be the Perfect Fit For You \n\n - You push relentlessly for reinvention: You're always asking \"how can this be better?\" -- in your work, in your craft, in yourself. Comfort is a signal to push harder, not coast. You'd rather build something better than defend something familiar.\n\n - You crave autonomy: We trust our team with big challenges and the freedom to solve them. If you’re someone who takes initiative, is comfortable taking risks, and seeks input when needed, you’ll find the freedom here empowering.\n\n - You own your work: You take pride in your work, follow through on commitments, and feel a deep sense of responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks.\n\n - You build with AI, not just use it: You're actively embedding AI into how you work, pushing what's possible, and bringing your team along with you.\n\n - You care about impact, not noise: You care deeply about the substance of your work. You measure success by results, not recognition, and you let your work speak for itself. \n\n - You’re energized by complexity and ambiguity: You enjoy tackling problems that don’t come with a playbook. You’re comfortable building from scratch, iterating as you go, and collaborating to shape the best path forward.\n\n - You seek out feedback: You see directness as respect, not criticism. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.\n\n\n\nAs Relay expands our Demand Generation strategy in 2026, we're investing in more targeted, coordinated ways to create and capture demand across our owned surfaces. We're looking for a Demand Generation Manager to own that work end to end.\n\n\n\nThis role sits within Demand Generation, and works alongside our broader marketing team. You'll own Relay's global lead engine from strategy through execution and results: the capture experiences across our site and content, the webinar and gated-content programming that earns attention, and the demo/chat experiences that turn interest into intent. You'll be the DRI for our lead number and how it converts. This is ideal for someone who spikes like a growth marketer rather than a channel specialist, defines success by quality rather than volume, and is energized by writing a playbook rather than following one.\n\n\n\nWhat You'll Be Doing\n\n - Own our global lead number end to end — set the strategy for how Relay captures demand across owned surfaces, and be accountable for how that demand progresses to demos and approvals\n\n - Build and run the lead programming calendar — the 12-month view and the quarterly plan, and run or coordinate each activation (webinars, gated ebooks and guides, partner programs, content offers)\n\n - Own the capture layer with our Web, CRO and MarOps teams — forms, enrichment, routing and testing — so lead quality holds as volume scales\n\n - Run our interactive demo and chatbot experiences — the \"see Relay\" layer for buyers who want to explore before they talk to anyone\n\n - Design and run experiments across the funnel — real hypotheses, holdout groups and kill criteria, then pull in the right teams to make winners bigger\n\n - Partner with Lifecycle to turn captured leads into demos, approvals and sales conversations, and own the feedback loop on lead quality\n\n - Turn what works into a repeatable motion and help shape how the broader marketing org treats leads as a first-class number\n\n\n\nWho You Are\n\n - You have 3–6 years of experience in B2B demand generation or integrated campaign management, and you've owned campaigns end to end — not just contributed to them\n\n - You're a quarterback, not a single-channel specialist. The Relay AppSec team genuinely enjoys Application Security and is looking to make an impact on the field.\n\n\n\nWhat You'll Be Doing\n\n - Threat modeling & offensive testing: Threat model technical design documents (TDDs) and run white-box penetration tests on our testing environment to identify vulnerabilities from an attacker’s point of view.\n\n - VDP & bug bounty: Triage researcher reports, reproduce/assess impact, coordinate fixes with owners, and close the loop with clear comms and durable controls.\n\n - Shipping the fixes you can: Contributing directly to Relay’s code base when it makes sense — writing the patch, not filing the ticket.\n\n - Working in our security tooling and extending it: Datadog security, secrets scanning and logging, Burp Suite, and in-house tools you'll be expected to modify rather than just operate.\n\n - Building with AI as a default: Claude Code and Cursor are daily drivers on this team, not a pilot program.\n\n - Joining the team's rhythms: Two weekly standups, a biweekly security champions session with product engineers, and a weekly Hack The Box session.\n\n - Software supply chain: Enforce provenance: SBOM on every build, dependency pinning/owner verification, private registries/proxies, and runtime SCA detections.\n\n\n\nWho You Are\n\n - You have 2 to 4 years of professional security experience. Application security, penetration testing, or product security engineering or similar roles.\n\n - You've shipped production code: Production-level software real users depended on. And you can read an unfamiliar codebase well enough to fix something in it, which is most of this job.\n\n - Security fundamentals: Deep understanding of OWASP Top 10 and real-world exploitation/mitigation techniques.\n\n - You build with AI. You use AI tooling in your daily work and you've built something with it. You can talk about where it gets things wrong, not just that it's fast.\n\n - Clear communicator & collaborator: you are a collaborator who loves to partner with developers to bring value to customers in the most secure way possible.\n\n - Ownership: You have a sense of responsibility towards problems and take ownership over them making sure nothing is forgotten and stakeholders stay informed.\n\n - Mentorship: You are comfortable mentoring team members and members of other teams on security best practices.\n\n\n\nThe Interview Process\n\n - Stage 1: A 60-minute Google Meet video call with the Hiring Manager\n\n - Stage 2: A 60-minute live session with the team\n\n - Stage 3: A 60-minute Secure Code Review and Coaching session with two members of our Customer Experience team\n\n - Stage 4: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with a member of our leadership team\n\n\n\nOur Compensation Approach\n\n\nWe believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth. Compensation follows impact. As impact increases, compensation grows, and we do not limit compensation changes to a once-a-year review cycle.\n\nThe annual salary range for this role is $126,000 CAD to $154,000 CAD.\n\nFor candidates who demonstrate full readiness for the defined scope of the role, the typical starting salary is $140,000 CAD. Offers below this point reflect candidates we believe can grow into the full scope of the role with support and development. Offers above this point reflect impact that meaningfully exceeds the role’s defined expectations or an expanded scope from day one.\n\nWe encourage you to have a conversation with your recruiter and ask questions about compensation throughout the hiring process. For more information on our compensation philosophy and perks and benefits, visit our Candidate Hub https://www.notion.so/Candidate-Hub-1c7da8b7f88580a893f7d7c7852b064e?pvs=21.\n\n\n\nWhy Relay Might Be the Perfect Fit For You \n\n - You push relentlessly for reinvention: You're always asking \"how can this be better?\" -- in your work, in your craft, in yourself. Comfort is a signal to push harder, not coast. You'd rather build something better than defend something familiar.\n\n - You crave autonomy: We trust our team with big challenges and the freedom to solve them. If you’re someone who takes initiative, is comfortable taking risks, and seeks input when needed, you’ll find the freedom here empowering.\n\n - You own your work: You take pride in your work, follow through on commitments, and feel a deep sense of responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks.\n\n - You build with AI, not just use it: You're actively embedding AI into how you work, pushing what's possible, and bringing your team along with you.\n\n - You care about impact, not noise: You care deeply about the substance of your work. You measure success by results, not recognition, and you let your work speak for itself. \n\n - You’re energized by complexity and ambiguity: You enjoy tackling problems that don’t come with a playbook. You’re comfortable building from scratch, iterating as you go, and collaborating to shape the best path forward.\n\n - You seek out feedback: You see directness as respect, not criticism. You actively seek input, sit with hard truths, and use feedback as fuel for improvement.\n\n - Small businesses are why we're here: Relay exists to help them thrive -- and that mission has to resonate with you.\n\n\n\nJoin Us\n\nWe're looking for people who are relentless, curious, and care deeply about the work. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Relay is scaling rapidly, and Compliance is the pillar that determines how fast we can scale safely. We've set ourselves ambitious goals for the next five years: growing transaction volume nearly 9x, launching credit and lending products, and expanding what we do for customers every single year. These are aspirations, not certainties — and hitting them depends on having a compliance program that is genuinely excellent. Not one that slows the business down, and not one that waves things through. We're looking for a leader who believes those two things are the same problem, solved with better data, better design, and better evidence — and who wants to be the person who helps us get there.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">As <strong>Director of Compliance</strong>, you'll own Compliance Strategy and Operations end-to-end: AML, sanctions, KYB/CDD, regulatory change, monitoring and testing, and the operational engine that runs it all. You'll own the compliance relationship with our sponsor bank — from day-to-day partnership through exams, audits, and new product approvals. And you'll build the team behind it, setting the standard for what \"good\" looks like as we grow.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">This is a build role, not a maintain role. The program you design becomes the thing that unlocks launch velocity with our banking partner, opens the door to banking-infrastructure optionality, and lets us bring products to market at the pace our customers need. You'll be building it with a Risk organization that is investing heavily in unified decision data, entity resolution, and agentic operations — which means your program can be evidence-driven and automated in ways that most compliance functions still only talk about.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">At Relay, your work has real reach — helping millions of SMBs operate safely and confidently, while protecting the integrity of our banking partnerships and our license to operate. If you want to build a modern compliance function from the ground up, with the mandate and the tooling to do it properly, this is the role for you.</p><h2><br />What You'll Be Doing</h2><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Own the Compliance Program:</strong> Build and own Relay's compliance program end-to-end — AML, sanctions, KYB/CDD, and regulatory compliance — including the policies, procedures, risk assessments, and controls that underpin it across every product and rail</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Program Governance:</strong> Be accountable for program effectiveness — investigations and suspicious activity governance, escalation paths, issue management through to validated remediation, and the internal standards that keep the program defensible</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Sponsor Bank Partnership:</strong> Own the compliance relationship with our sponsor bank — day-to-day partnership, exam and audit readiness, issue resolution, product approvals, and the management information package that demonstrates our control environment</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Build an Evidence Engine:</strong> Design the monitoring, testing, and reporting infrastructure that lets us prove control effectiveness with data rather than assertion — producing a complete, examination-grade customer risk picture in hours, not weeks</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Financial Crimes Strategy:</strong> Set the strategy for transaction monitoring, investigation, and suspicious activity reporting — designing detection that meets the highest regulatory standard while keeping legitimate customers moving</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Perpetual KYB &amp; Customer Diligence:</strong> Move us from periodic review to continuous re-verification — ownership drift, entity status, industry change, adverse media — with a particular eye on synthetic business identity, the fastest-growing attack on SMB fintech</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Enable the Business:</strong> Partner with Product, Engineering, Risk, and Operations to embed compliance requirements into new products and features from the design stage, so compliance becomes a design input rather than a launch gate</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Regulatory Change Management:</strong> Track the regulatory landscape — FinCEN program effectiveness expectations, Nacha fraud monitoring obligations, sanctions developments, post-Synapse sponsor oversight — and translate change into concrete updates to our controls and roadmap</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Build and Lead the Team:</strong> Hire, coach, and grow the Compliance pillar across both strategy and operations. Set the structure, the career paths, and the standard of work</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Scale Operations Without Scaling Headcount Linearly:</strong> Push AI and automation into compliance operations so agents assemble evidence, summarize, and draft while your team disposition, contain, and attest — capacity grows with volume, headcount grows with judgment</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Measure What Matters:</strong> Run the pillar on a paired scorecard — risk outcomes alongside customer friction — so we never buy compliance performance with unnecessary customer disruption, or vice versa</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Board and Leadership Reporting:</strong> Provide clear, periodic reporting to senior management and the board on program health, emerging risk, and issue remediation</p></li></ul><h2>Who You Are</h2><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You have 8+ years of compliance experience in fintech, banking, or payments, including time leading a compliance function or a major pillar of one</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You've built compliance programs, policies, and control frameworks from the ground up — not just inherited and maintained them</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You've owned a program's effectiveness personally, and you understand the difference between a program that looks compliant and one that holds up under scrutiny</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You've managed a sponsor bank, regulator, or examiner relationship directly, and you know that credibility is built between exams, not during them</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You lead through data. You've said no when it mattered, and more often you've found the path to yes that nobody else could see</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You're a strong communicator across every altitude — a board deck, a bank exam response, an engineering ticket, and a hard conversation with a product leader</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You thrive in fast-paced environments, tackling We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.\n\nRelay is scaling rapidly, and Compliance is the pillar that determines how fast we can scale safely. We've set ourselves ambitious goals for the next five years: growing transaction volume nearly 9x, launching credit and lending products, and expanding what we do for customers every single year. These are aspirations, not certainties — and hitting them depends on having a compliance program that is genuinely excellent. Not one that slows the business down, and not one that waves things through. We're looking for a leader who believes those two things are the same problem, solved with better data, better design, and better evidence — and who wants to be the person who helps us get there.\n\nAs Director of Compliance, you'll own Compliance Strategy and Operations end-to-end: AML, sanctions, KYB/CDD, regulatory change, monitoring and testing, and the operational engine that runs it all. You'll own the compliance relationship with our sponsor bank — from day-to-day partnership through exams, audits, and new product approvals. And you'll build the team behind it, setting the standard for what \"good\" looks like as we grow.\n\nThis is a build role, not a maintain role. The program you design becomes the thing that unlocks launch velocity with our banking partner, opens the door to banking-infrastructure optionality, and lets us bring products to market at the pace our customers need. You'll be building it with a Risk organization that is investing heavily in unified decision data, entity resolution, and agentic operations — which means your program can be evidence-driven and automated in ways that most compliance functions still only talk about.\n\nAt Relay, your work has real reach — helping millions of SMBs operate safely and confidently, while protecting the integrity of our banking partnerships and our license to operate. If you want to build a modern compliance function from the ground up, with the mandate and the tooling to do it properly, this is the role for you.\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU'LL BE DOING\n\n - Own the Compliance Program: Build and own Relay's compliance program end-to-end — AML, sanctions, KYB/CDD, and regulatory compliance — including the policies, procedures, risk assessments, and controls that underpin it across every product and rail\n\n - Program Governance: Be accountable for program effectiveness — investigations and suspicious activity governance, escalation paths, issue management through to validated remediation, and the internal standards that keep the program defensible\n\n - Sponsor Bank Partnership: Own the compliance relationship with our sponsor bank — day-to-day partnership, exam and audit readiness, issue resolution, product approvals, and the management information package that demonstrates our control environment\n\n - Build an Evidence Engine: Design the monitoring, testing, and reporting infrastructure that lets us prove control effectiveness with data rather than assertion — producing a complete, examination-grade customer risk picture in hours, not weeks\n\n - Financial Crimes Strategy: Set the strategy for transaction monitoring, investigation, and suspicious activity reporting — designing detection that meets the highest regulatory standard while keeping legitimate customers moving\n\n - Perpetual KYB & Customer Diligence: Move us from periodic review to continuous re-verification — ownership drift, entity status, industry change, adverse media — with a particular eye on synthetic business identity, the fastest-growing attack on SMB fintech\n\n - Enable the Business: Partner with Product, Engineering, Risk, and Operations to embed compliance requirements into new products and features from the design stage, so compliance becomes a design input rather than a launch gate\n\n - Regulatory Change Management: Track the regulatory landscape — FinCEN program effectiveness expectations, Nacha fraud monitoring obligations, sanctions developments, post-Synapse sponsor oversight — and translate change into concrete updates to our controls and roadmap\n\n - Build and Lead the Team: Hire, coach, and grow the Compliance pillar across both strategy and operations. Set the structure, the career paths, and the standard of work\n\n - Scale Operations Without Scaling Headcount Linearly: Push AI and automation into compliance operations so agents assemble evidence, summarize, and draft while your team disposition, contain, and attest — capacity grows with volume, headcount grows with judgment\n\n - Measure What Matters: Run the pillar on a paired scorecard — risk outcomes alongside customer friction — so we never buy compliance performance with unnecessary customer disruption, or vice versa\n\n - Board and Leadership Reporting: Provide clear, periodic reporting to senior management and the board on program health, emerging risk, and issue remediation\n\n\nWHO YOU ARE\n\n - You have 8+ years of compliance experience in fintech, banking, or payments, including time leading a compliance function or a major pillar of one\n\n - You've built compliance programs, policies, and control frameworks from the ground up — not just inherited and maintained them\n\n - You've owned a program's effectiveness personally, and you understand the difference between a program that looks compliant and one that holds up under scrutiny\n\n - You've managed a sponsor bank, regulator, or examiner relationship directly, and you know that credibility is built between exams, not during them\n\n - You lead through data. You're comfortable defining the metrics that prove a control works, and you'd rather show a regulator a dataset than a memo\n\n - You're technically fluent enough to be dangerous — you can reason about how monitoring systems, decisioning platforms, and data pipelines actually work, and you can hold your own with Engineering on what needs to be logged and why\n\n - You've hired, coached, and grown compliance talent, and you're energized by building a team's standard rather than just its output\n\n - You genuinely believe compliance enables growth. You've said no when it mattered, and more often you've found the path to yes that nobody else could see\n\n - You're a strong communicator across every altitude — a board deck, a bank exam response, an engineering ticket, and a hard conversation with a product leader\n\n - You thrive in fast-paced environments, tackling ambiguity, building process where none exists, and raising the bar across the team\n\n - You're actively using AI tools in how you work today and you're excited to push what's possible with them\n\n\nBONUS POINTS\n\n - You have experience with charter applications, second sponsor bank diligence, or banking-as-a-service program structuring\n\n - You're familiar with compliance and financial crimes tooling like Unit21, Sardine, Alloy, Middesk, Hawk, or similar\n\n - You have experience across multiple product types — deposits, cards, ACH, RDC, acquiring, or credit\n\n - You've joined a company at its early stages and have seen it through scale\n\n - You have experience working in a fintech startup or scale-up\n\n\nTHE INTERVIEW PROCESS\n\n - Stage 1: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with a member of the Talent team\n\n - Stage 2: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with the Head of Risk\n\n - Stage 3: A take-home case study followed by a 60-minute Google Meet video call with our Risk leadership team\n\n - Stage 4: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with a cross-functional partner (Product, Engineering, or Operations)\n\n - Stage 5: A 45-minute in-person interview with a member of the Executive team\n\n\nOUR COMPENSATION APPROACH\n\nWe believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth. You’re a lifelong learner, curious about new frameworks, best practices, and emerging technologies\n\n - You thrive in fast-paced, dynamic environments and are comfortable navigating ambiguity and change\n\n - You’re a collaborative team player, eager to pitch in, ask questions, and provide and receive feedback\n\n - You take ownership end-to-end, solving problems creatively and proactively, while keeping the customer and business impact front-of-mind\n\n \n\nIt’s a bonus (but not required) if you\n\n - Have worked in startups or high-growth tech companies\n\n - Have hands-on experience building with LLMs, including self-hosting or serving open models, retrieval systems, evaluation, or agentic workflows\n\n - Have built platform or shared services used by other engineering teams\n\n - Have experience with JavaScript - we primarily use TypeScript, React, and Node.js\n\n - Have working knowledge of AWS services (ECS, S3, RDS, Dynamo, Lambda) and continuous deployment pipelines\n\n \n\nOur Tech Stack\n\n - Front-end: React, Typescript, React Native\n\n - Back-end: Node.js, Typescript, Terraform, AWS (DynamoDB, RDS Postgres, Lambda, S3, SQS, SNS, SES, ElasticSearch, ECS)\n\n - Tools: Cursor, Claude, GitHub, GitHub Actions, Datadog, Jira, Metabase\n\n \n\nThe Interview Process\n\n - Stage 4: A take-home system design challenge, followed by a 60-minute Google Meet video call review with two members of the Engineering team\n\n - Stage 5: A 45-minute in-person interview with a member of the Leadership team\n\n \n\nOur Compensation Approach\n\nWe believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth. Compensation follows impact. As impact increases, compensation grows, and we do not limit compensation changes to a once-a-year review cycle.\n\n \n\nThe annual salary range for this role is $144,000 CAD to $176,000 CAD.\n\n \n\nFor candidates who demonstrate full readiness for the defined scope of the role, the typical starting salary is $160,000 CAD. Offers below this point reflect candidates we believe can grow into the full scope of the role with support and development. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You'll join <strong>Core Banking</strong>, the team building the resilient banking infrastructure that Relay's customers and internal teams depend on — ACH and wire transfers, local and international, and everything that keeps money moving securely and predictably. Core and Risk Engineering are tied at the hip, and you'll be embedded across both. The team's north star is simple: <strong>scalable, reliable, on time, under budget</strong> — measured in escaped defects, test flakiness and duration, incident count, and uptime.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Your mission is to scale quality operations and build the tooling, frameworks and CI pipelines for a distributed system that make it easy to scale quality and increase development velocity across every engineering team at Relay.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">This is not a role where you write UI tests against someone else's system. You will have the same leverage as a developer.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>What You'll Be Doing</strong></p><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Own the quality roadmap for Risk Engineering</strong> and build the quality engineering frameworks for Core Banking systems, including ACH and domestic and international wire transfers.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Build and improve our CI infrastructure</strong>, including the migration to ministack — testing lambdas and microservices in CI with local implementations of Wiremock, Localstack and PSQL. You'll be measured on the same numbers the team is: escaped defects, test flakiness and duration, incident count, uptime.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Drive shift-left across the teams you're embedded in</strong> — attending sprint ceremonies and getting developers writing tests as part of their deliverables, not as a handoff to QA.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Find and remove the bottlenecks in quality operations</strong>, diagnosing pain points across Core Banking and Risk and championing the solutions.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Build tools that improve developer experience</strong>, with minimal dependency on third parties.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Mentor junior quality engineers</strong> and contribute to the direction and larger-scale initiatives of the Quality Engineering team.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Tell the quality story with data</strong> — gathering defect and quality data from across our systems and presenting it to engineering leadership and executives.</p></li></ul><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Roughly 75% of your week is hands-on building. The other 25% is influence: ceremonies, mentorship, evangelism, and getting teams to adopt what you've built.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Who You Are</strong></p><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You have built quality engineering systems from the ground up, hands on</strong> — frameworks, test suites and CI systems, not just tests written against someone else's harness.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You have tested distributed systems</strong>, not only UIs. Services, lambdas, microservices, real-time applications — you understand what makes them hard to test and you've done it in CI.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You understand and care deeply about system architecture</strong> - you have an in depth understanding of how a distributed system is architected - how systems communicate, how scaleability and resilience is built into a system and how to design tests for these complex systems instead of treating them like a black box.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You can influence and persuade development teams to adopt quality practices.</strong> You've changed how a team works, not just what you shipped.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You debug from first principles</strong>, using code, logs and traces to get to genuine root cause.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You can gather quality and defect data from multiple sources and present it to a wide audience</strong>, including executives, and make the numbers mean something.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You are AI-fluent in practice</strong> — using AI tools daily, comfortable with how agents We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.\n\n\n\nYou'll join Core Banking, the team building the resilient banking infrastructure that Relay's customers and internal teams depend on — ACH and wire transfers, local and international, and everything that keeps money moving securely and predictably. Core and Risk Engineering are tied at the hip, and you'll be embedded across both. The team's north star is simple: scalable, reliable, on time, under budget — measured in escaped defects, test flakiness and duration, incident count, and uptime.\n\nYour mission is to scale quality operations and build the tooling, frameworks and CI pipelines for a distributed system that make it easy to scale quality and increase development velocity across every engineering team at Relay.\n\nThis is not a role where you write UI tests against someone else's system. You will have the same leverage as a developer.\n\n\n\nWhat You'll Be Doing\n\n - Own the quality roadmap for Risk Engineering and build the quality engineering frameworks for Core Banking systems, including ACH and domestic and international wire transfers.\n\n - Build and improve our CI infrastructure, including the migration to ministack — testing lambdas and microservices in CI with local implementations of Wiremock, Localstack and PSQL. You'll be measured on the same numbers the team is: escaped defects, test flakiness and duration, incident count, uptime.\n\n - Drive shift-left across the teams you're embedded in — attending sprint ceremonies and getting developers writing tests as part of their deliverables, not as a handoff to QA.\n\n - Find and remove the bottlenecks in quality operations, diagnosing pain points across Core Banking and Risk and championing the solutions.\n\n - Build tools that improve developer experience, with minimal dependency on third parties.\n\n - Mentor junior quality engineers and contribute to the direction and larger-scale initiatives of the Quality Engineering team.\n\n - Tell the quality story with data — gathering defect and quality data from across our systems and presenting it to engineering leadership and executives.\n\nRoughly 75% of your week is hands-on building. The other 25% is influence: ceremonies, mentorship, evangelism, and getting teams to adopt what you've built.\n\n\n\nWho You Are\n\n - You have built quality engineering systems from the ground up, hands on — frameworks, test suites and CI systems, not just tests written against someone else's harness.\n\n - You have tested distributed systems, not only UIs. Services, lambdas, microservices, real-time applications — you understand what makes them hard to test and you've done it in CI.\n\n - You understand and care deeply about system architecture - you have an in depth understanding of how a distributed system is architected - how systems communicate, how scaleability and resilience is built into a system and how to design tests for these complex systems instead of treating them like a black box.\n\n - You can influence and persuade development teams to adopt quality practices. You've changed how a team works, not just what you shipped.\n\n - You debug from first principles, using code, logs and traces to get to genuine root cause.\n\n - You can gather quality and defect data from multiple sources and present it to a wide audience, including executives, and make the numbers mean something.\n\n - You are AI-fluent in practice — using AI tools daily, comfortable with how agents work and with the systems underneath them, and able to critique AI output rather than accept it blindly.\n\n - You thrive in agile teams that move quickly and you're comfortable with ambiguity and abstract requirements.\n\nBonus Points\n\n - Mobile testing experience (Detox).\n\n - Experience with AWS systems.\n\nOur stack: React, Nodejs, AWS Infrastructure (Queues, S3, DynamoDB etc.) , PSQL, Redis, Playwright, Detox, GitHub Actions, Ministack/Localstack, Wiremock, Bruno, Sentry, Datadog, Cursor, Claude, JIRA, Notion.\n\n\n\nThe Interview Process\n\n - Stage 1: A 30-minute Google Meet video call with a member of our Engineering Team\n\n - Stage 2: A 60-minute Google Meet with the Hiring Manager\n\n - Stage 3: A 90-minute technical interview and case study with members of the hiring team \n\n - Stage 4: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with a member of our leadership team\n\n\n\nOur Compensation Approach\n\nWe believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth.
